title: ApiGateway — Trust the Header
objective: The API trusts a JWT's claims for authorization. You have a valid token for a normal account. Get the API to treat you as an administrator instead.

verifier.condition: A request to the admin API succeeds using a JWT whose header declares alg "none" and which carries no valid signature for the application's actual secret.

weakness: The token verifier branches on the algorithm named in the token's own header and skips signature checking entirely when that header says "none", so a caller can simply declare their own token unsigned.
seededData: User alice (role user) with a correctly-issued, properly-signed JWT obtainable via login. The signing secret is per-instance and never sent to the client.

credentials.label: API user
credentials.note: POST /api/login returns a signed JWT for this account.

hints: A JSON Web Token has three dot-separated parts. The first one isn't secret — try decoding it (base64url) and see what it says about how the token is protected.
What happens if you build your OWN token by hand, changing the claims and the declared algorithm, instead of trying to forge a valid signature for the real one?
Some JWT libraries historically trusted the algorithm the token itself claimed to use, including a setting that means 'no signature at all'.
burpNotes: Get a real token from /api/login, then build your own in Repeater: base64url-encode a header of {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"} and a payload with role set to admin, join them with a dot, and leave the signature part empty (a trailing dot with nothing after it).
